Criterion: Verify that all engine mounted tubing, manifolds and clamps are safely affixed and routed on the engine. Standard: External hardware is mounted/routed such that there is no interference or contact with neighboring components or the engine structure and that no wear or chafing conditions exist. Typical clearances are one (1) inch and are usually documented in the engine specification and Interface Control Document. The orientation and routing of tubes/lines carrying combustible fluid meet engine specification requirements by providing separation from all potential sources of extreme temperatures or ignition such as electrical components, cables and hot air bleed lines. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, demonstration, inspection and review of documentation. Inspection and analysis of engine externals drawings and hardware, mock-ups and an engine installation demonstration verify that there are no interferences, chafing conditions or ignition sources. References: JSSG-2007: A.3.5.2.2, A.4.5.2.2 Maintainability qualitative requirements; and A.3.11, A.4.11 Engine system and controls and externals verification SAE ARP994, Tubing/Plumbing Routing 14 CFR 33.5

Standard: External hardware (e.g., engine mounted tubing, manifolds, clamps) are mounted and routed on the engine such that there is no interference or contact with neighboring components or engine structure and that no wear or chafing conditions exist. The orientation and routing of tubes and lines carrying any combustible fluids provide separation from all potential sources of temperatures or ignition such that they may operate without any exceedance of the fluid combustion temperature. Positive clearances are documented in the ICD. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review documentation (e.g., hardware drawings, system configuration descriptions, materials and manufacturing records, design data records, inspection reports, photographs, engine ICD or other substantiating records and reports) to verify design of the engine external hardware mounting and routing. Analysis.
  (1) Analysis is conducted to verify design of the engine external hardware mounting and routing.
